en.isp_notice_title: CRUCIAL ADVISORY: Older Records May Be Missing from MyCase
en.isp_notice_desc: Indiana courts rolled out the Odyssey computer system between 2005 and 2011. Older paper cases, pre-2010 dispositions, unfiled arrests, and juvenile records may NOT appear on MyCase. Because of Indiana's Lifetime One-Shot Rule (IC § 35-38-9-9(i)), omitting an older conviction permanently forfeits your right to expunge it.

en.explainer_title: What Does Indiana Expungement Actually Do? (Statutory Tiers & Non-Eligible Offenses)
en.explainer_sec1_desc: Arrests without conviction, dismissed charges, or acquittals. Completely seals records from public view. Exempt from the lifetime one-shot rule.
en.explainer_sec23_desc: Mandatory expungement if statutory requirements and waiting periods (5 or 8 years) are met. Court SHALL grant the petition.
en.explainer_sec45_desc: Levels 1–5 felonies. Discretionary expungement; marked as expunged on public records rather than fully sealed. Requires prosecutor consent for serious injury.
en.explainer_barred_desc: Homicide, sex/violent offender registry offenses, human trafficking, and official misconduct are statutorily barred under IC § 35-38-9-8(b).

en.address_statutory_title: Why Does Indiana Law Require Your Full Address History?
en.address_statutory_p1: Under IC § 35-38-9-8(b)(3), your petition must list every residential address where you have lived from the date of your earliest arrest or offense to the present:
en.address_statutory_b1: Prosecutorial Verification: The Prosecutor and Indiana State Police use this history to check local law enforcement records and confirm no active warrants or pending charges exist in any jurisdiction where you lived.
en.address_statutory_b2: Confidential Protection (Form ACR): All address history is filed under Indiana Rules on Access to Court Records (Rule 5) on Form ACR, keeping your past and current addresses sealed from the public.
en.address_statutory_b3: Avoiding Pleading Defects: Omitting a prior residence is a statutory defect that prosecutors can raise to delay or object to your expungement.

es.explainer_sec1_desc: Arrestos sin condena, cargos desestimados o absoluciones. Sella completamente los registros de la vista pública. Exento de la regla de una sola vez de por vida.

es.explainer_sec45_desc: Delitos graves niveles 1 a 5. Eliminación discrecional; marcados como eliminados en registros públicos en lugar de sellarse por completo. Requiere el consentimiento del fiscal para lesiones graves.
es.explainer_barred_desc: El homicidio, delitos del registro de delincuentes sexuales/violentos, trata de personas y mala conducta de funcionarios están legalmente prohibidos según IC § 35-38-9-8(b).

es.address_statutory_p1: Bajo IC § 35-38-9-8(b)(3), su petición debe enumerar cada dirección residencial donde ha vivido desde la fecha de su primer arresto o delito hasta el presente:
es.address_statutory_b1: Verificación de la Fiscalía: El Fiscal y la Policía Estatal de Indiana usan este historial para verificar los registros policiales locales y confirmar que no existan órdenes de arresto activas ni cargos pendientes en ninguna jurisdicción donde vivió.
es.address_statutory_b2: Protección Confidencial (Formulario ACR): Todo el historial de direcciones se presenta bajo la Regla 5 de Acceso a Registros Judiciales de Indiana en el Formulario ACR, manteniendo sus direcciones anteriores y actuales selladas del público.
es.address_statutory_b3: Evitar Defectos en el Escrito: Omitir una residencia anterior es un defecto legal que los fiscales pueden señalar para retrasar u objetar su eliminación de antecedentes.
